paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, promotion, search entry, and automatic login-overlay archetype.
Search/listing archetype for the core product-discovery journey, including filters and long-page scrolling.
Representative product-detail archetype with pricing, variants, offers, metadata, and product imagery.
Authentication/form archetype, including empty submission, validation feedback, and mobile reflow.
Empty-cart and recovery state in the shopping journey.
Representative 404 response and recovery page, observed at /sitemap.xml.

findings.summary: The interface remains light under a dark system preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-scheme screenshot is visually the same light white/grey UI as the default, and the fetched 458 KB CSS contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven surface/text tokens, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found five running animations, including durations of 4.72 s and 5.33 s; CSS feature inspection found no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation and auto-advance inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: No authored high-contrast adaptation is present.
findings.evidence: Fetched CSS contains no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; the increased-contrast capture does not establish a purpose-built high-contrast treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for controls, focus indicators, and custom chrome.

findings.summary: Route and modal state changes do not use authored View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across home, search, and product found zero view-transition declarations; the modal-cycle video shows an abrupt custom state swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for modal/state changes and cross-document transitions for compatible route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listing navigation does not provide scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The listing scroll video and CSS inspection show no progress indicator, shrinking header, scroll-state query, or equivalent positional feedback on a 10,183 px page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or state-aware sticky header using declarative scroll-state techniques.

findings.summary: Menus and the login overlay are manually positioned rather than anchored.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try declarations on the sampled templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for menus and transient UI near viewport edges.

findings.summary: A login interstitial obscures the homepage on load.
findings.evidence: The desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show a dimmed page covered by a large login prompt before user intent; on mobile the overlay is clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open authentication on load. Trigger it from an explicit user action and retain an obvious dismiss path.

findings.summary: The login modal is an unlabelled custom div, not a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM/probe evidence reports dialog=0, ariaModal=0 and a full-viewport custom DIV while the screenshot clearly shows modal behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the flow with <dialog>, accessible naming, focus trapping/restoration, Escape and platform dismissal.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome and the account prompt crowd out shopping content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport is dominated by the account modal, header categories, and ad creative; core product content is mostly obscured.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the automatic modal and reduce competing first-viewport promotion so search and products remain primary.

findings.summary: Search and login templates ship a 980 px desktop viewport to 360 px devices.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reports clientWidth=980, scale=0.367 and hasViewportMeta=false for search and login, making text and controls tiny; the homepage modal also scrolls to 370 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid responsive viewport on every template and rebuild fixed desktop grids/forms with intrinsic fluid layouts. Do not disable zoom.

findings.summary: Shared search/auth components do not adapt consistently by container.
findings.evidence: Search/login render as scaled desktop pages while product/cart use true 360 px layouts; all three CSS probes report zero @container/container-type usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Make shared header, filters, cards, and auth panel container-responsive and test each template at narrow sizes.

findings.summary: Many controls are undersized and several suppress focus indication.
findings.evidence: The home probe found 42/96 visible interactive targets under 44 px; search found 50/88. Focused search inputs/buttons computed outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet touch target spacing/sizing and provide clear :focus-visible styles without removing the native outline unless replaced.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading misses the good LCP and responsiveness bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.0 s, TBT 470 ms, Speed Index 7.7 s and interactive 18.1 s (performance 0.65).
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element, reduce startup JavaScript, and schedule non-critical work after interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Product and cart views shift materially after load.
findings.evidence: The layout observer measured CLS 0.083 on product and 0.106 on cart, with the cart shift concentrated in a 0.106 event.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content and stabilise image, offer, and empty-state dimensions before paint.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse TBT was 470 ms; traces found 3 long tasks on both home and product, and the product trace recorded 120 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, defer non-critical modules, and schedule analytics/background work at lower priority.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is script-heavy.
findings.evidence: The home HAR records 123 requests and 3.44 MB transferred, including 2.81 MB of script; product transfers 3.31 MB with 2.86 MB script. Parser-initiated modules were confirmed deferred, leaving the stylesheet and sheer startup graph as the concern.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the critical dependency graph, preload only proven critical assets, and improve caching for stable bundles.

findings.summary: Large legacy and instrumentation bundles dominate page weight.
findings.evidence: Home loads 27 script requests/2.81 MB and search still loads polyfills plus analytics/tag-manager scripts; script is over 80% of transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage and bundle analysis to remove unused/duplicate code, conditionally load legacy support, and gate instrumentation.

findings.summary: Core controls and images lack accessible names or labels.
findings.evidence: axe found 14 missing image alternatives, critical unlabeled form elements, and three unnamed links on home; login has an unnamed button, unlabeled input, ten images without alt, and four unnamed links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels and programmatic names, meaningful alt text, and correct button/link semantics.

findings.summary: Text and links fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: axe reported five contrast failures on home and twenty on login, including form/help text and policy links; Lighthouse also failed color-contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust color tokens to meet WCAG AA in default, hover, focus, disabled, and error states.

findings.summary: Landmarks and visible focus are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The product has no main landmark and duplicate contentinfo landmarks; home has no main/nav landmarks. Focus probes show outline:none on search fields and many links across search/login.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single main landmark, unique landmarks, logical headings, and strong :focus-visible treatment in DOM order.

findings.summary: Desktop scaling makes mobile listing and login text illegible.
findings.evidence: The 360 px search capture scales a 980 px, 10,183 px desktop page to 36.7%, and the login capture similarly miniaturises the whole form/footer.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography and reflowed single-column layouts rather than viewport-scale shrinkage.

findings.summary: Several templates prevent zoom or omit the responsive viewport.
findings.evidence: Home/product declare user-scalable=no; search/login omit viewport meta and render at 980 px. axe flags the viewport setting as critical.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no, add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 consistently, and verify 200% zoom/reflow.

findings.summary: The homepage emits failed network requests in the console.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded three console failures: one 401 unread-count request and two 406 analytics collector requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid unauthenticated requests that predictably fail and suppress/retry telemetry only when valid.

findings.summary: Many images lack intrinsic dimensions and use legacy formats.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 45/97 homepage images and 18/64 product images without dimensions; 54 homepage images use legacy formats and six are oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve correct aspect ratios, and serve efficient modern formats at responsive sizes.

findings.summary: Rendered representative pages do not expose meta descriptions consistently.
findings.evidence: Direct DOM probes found meta[name=description] absent on home, search, product, login, and cart, although titles were descriptive; Lighthouse observed a homepage description in a separate run, indicating inconsistent output.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit stable, unique descriptions in server HTML for public templates and retain them after hydration.

findings.summary: Public listing pages are not mobile-friendly and one anchor is not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Search has no viewport meta and is scaled to 980 px; Lighthouse found one non-crawlable anchor and the live home probe found one anchor without href.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide real hrefs and a responsive viewport on every public template; keep descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie flags are weaker than expected.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and CSP are present, but HSTS and nosniff are missing; CSP permits unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval. Cookie audit reports 14 SameSite=None cookies and 8 without Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS and nosniff, tighten CSP away from unsafe directives, and mark cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Analytics and third-party activity are broad for an anonymous first load.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found eight cross-origin origins and active New Relic endpoints; the HAR attributes 121/123 requests and 3.27 MB to other origins (mostly Flipkart CDNs, plus monitoring).
findings.suggestedFix: Classify corporate CDNs separately, then minimise monitoring/marketing collection, batch events, and load non-essential analytics after consent or need.

findings.summary: Login offers OTP only, with no visible passkey route.
findings.evidence: The sampled login page requests email/mobile and Request OTP; no password is collected, but no WebAuthn/passkey option or credential affordance appears. No permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys as the preferred phishing-resistant sign-in path while retaining OTP recovery.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff, and CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS and nosniff; adopt nonces/hashes and Trusted Types where feasible.

findings.summary: The custom login overlay is clipped on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The 360 px homepage capture shows the modal extending beyond both sides, with its left content and create-account action cut off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic responsive dialog constrained with logical insets/max-size and test focus/dismissal at viewport edges.

findings.summary: The commerce experience is not installable from the sampled pages.
findings.evidence: Home/product/search probes found no link rel=manifest; no install surface was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a valid web app manifest and an intentional offline fallback for navigation and saved/cart state where business rules permit.

findings.summary: International layout support is incomplete.
findings.evidence: lang is present (en/en-IN), but fetched CSS across representative templates contains zero logical margin/padding/inset properties and no authored dir adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt logical properties and verify translated/RTL layouts; set dir explicitly when locale direction can vary.

findings.summary: Authentication is nagged before the user asks for it.
findings.evidence: The homepage opens the login prompt automatically over product content, while login is also available in the header; this creates an avoidable account-pressure interruption.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep anonymous browsing unobstructed and ask for authentication only at an action that requires it.

findings.summary: Login errors are visible but not exposed as invalid state.
findings.evidence: After empty Request OTP, text says “Please enter valid Email ID/Mobile number”, but every sampled input still has aria-invalid=null, :user-invalid=false, and no native validationMessage.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate the message with the field, set aria-invalid after interaction, and announce the error through an appropriate live region.

findings.summary: Sign-in and search inputs disable autocomplete and lack visible labels.
findings.evidence: Login probe shows the identity field with autocomplete=off and no label/aria-label; search fields also use autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a visible label and the correct username/email/tel and one-time-code autocomplete tokens; do not disable autofill.

findings.summary: Image delivery still wastes bytes and layout certainty.
findings.evidence: Homepage image audit found 54 legacy-format images, six oversized images, and 45 without dimensions; product found 28 legacy and three oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where appropriate, right-size responsive sources, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Anonymous loads perform avoidable failing and analytics work.
findings.evidence: The homepage makes 123 requests including 25 fetch/XHR; Lighthouse logs a predictable 401 and two 406 collector calls, while traces record repeated long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove predictable failing calls, batch telemetry, and deprioritise background collection until idle/consent.

findings.summary: The startup budget is dominated by cross-origin scripts.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 3.27 MB/3.44 MB and 121/123 homepage requests from origins other than www.flipkart.com; 2.81 MB is script and New Relic tracking is active. Most byte-heavy origins are Flipkart CDNs, but they still consume user resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit script/third-party budget, defer monitoring, and cache/version CDN assets aggressively.

findings.summary: High-value commerce actions are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The product is reasonably crawlable and has JSON-LD, but no WebMCP/agentic form registration was observed on search, product, login, or cart.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose narrowly scoped, user-confirmed search/cart capabilities through WebMCP when support and risk controls are ready.

taskList.title: Repair mobile viewport, zoom, and true reflow across search/login/home dialog
Remove the automatic login interruption and rebuild it as an accessible responsive dialog
Fix accessible names, labels, landmarks, focus, contrast, and touch targets
Cut startup JavaScript and main-thread work to meet LCP/TBT targets
Harden response headers, CSP, and cookie attributes
Add dark, reduced-motion, and high-contrast preference adaptations
Stabilise image dimensions and modernise asset delivery
Make login validation and autofill assistive and announce errors
Reduce anonymous telemetry, failing calls, and cross-origin script budget
Stabilise SEO descriptions, crawlable links, and mobile metadata
